name: Filesystem Analysis
description: Ability to analyse filesystem structures across NTFS, ext4, APFS, HFS+, FAT32, and exFAT. Covers parsing Master File Table (MFT), inode structures, journal analysis, alternate data streams, file system metadata, and identifying evidence of anti-forensic manipulation.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to forensic filesystem analysis

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands basic filesystem concepts and why filesystem metadata is forensically significant
evidence: Can describe the major filesystem types and their forensic relevance
Understands concepts of file allocation, slack space, and unallocated space
Can explain why timestamps and metadata are important evidence

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Navigates and examines filesystem structures using forensic tools under supervision
evidence: Parsed NTFS MFT entries and extracted file metadata using Autopsy or X-Ways
Identified alternate data streams in NTFS volumes under guidance
Examined ext4 inode structures and journal entries with supervisor review
Located files in unallocated space using keyword and signature searches

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently analyses filesystem structures across Windows, Linux, and macOS evidence and produces forensic reports
evidence: Independently analysed filesystems in 5+ cases across NTFS, ext4, and APFS
Correctly identified timestomping and other anti-forensic filesystem manipulation
Correlated filesystem journal entries with user activity to establish timelines
Produced filesystem analysis reports that withstood technical and legal review

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex multi-filesystem and damaged volume analysis; identifies sophisticated anti-forensic techniques
evidence: Analysed complex multi-partition and multi-OS boot configurations
Recovered evidence from partially overwritten or corrupted filesystems
Detected sophisticated anti-forensic techniques including journal manipulation
Reviews filesystem analysis work products of junior examiners
Developed custom parsing scripts for non-standard filesystem artifacts

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines filesystem analysis methodology; researches new filesystem internals; provides expert testimony
evidence: Authored or maintains lab filesystem analysis procedures for multiple OS types
Published research on filesystem artifact interpretation or anti-forensic detection
Validated forensic tool accuracy against filesystem specifications
Provides expert testimony on filesystem evidence interpretation

assessment_methods.description: Analyse prepared disk images containing filesystem artifacts across NTFS, ext4, and APFS, identify anti-forensic manipulation, and produce a findings report
Review filesystem analysis sections from recent case reports for accuracy and completeness
